biodiversity_overview.text: 32,823 GBIF occurrence records for 84 tracked species are attributed to West Bengal, spanning 1828-2026.
32,179 of these records (98.0%) are located to within 10 km.

species_richness.text: Observed tracked species by group: Aves 27, Magnoliopsida 16, Mammalia 14, Actinopterygii 10, Squamata 7, Testudines 5, Amphibia 4, Crocodylia 1.

threatened_species.text: 9 species with records here are officially threatened (IUCN CR/EN/VU). Names and categories from the IUCN Red List export are not shown in this public snapshot.
4 further species are threatened according to the project's unverified reference list: Tiger (EN), Asian Elephant (EN), Indian Rhinoceros (VU), Mugger Crocodile (VU).

notable_species.text: Most recorded species: Indian Pied Starling (11,931), Indian Pond-heron (2,922), Indian Cormorant (2,474), Indian Cuckoo (2,138), Indian Golden Oriole (1,601).

temporal_trends.text: Records per year went from 492 in 2016 to 263 in 2025. This reflects recording effort as much as wildlife and is not a population trend.

protection_coverage.text: Wildlife protected areas (OpenStreetMap national parks, sanctuaries and reserves) cover 3.09% of West Bengal's area (23 areas intersect the state).
6.0% of precisely located records fall inside these areas (1,920 of 32,179); this is not a measure of habitat protection.

risk_indicators.text: Highest model-predicted vulnerability among species recorded here (MODEL PREDICTION, not IUCN status): Carplet (0.55), Peacock Soft-shelled Turtle (0.50), Indian Softshell Turtle (0.49), Indian Spotted Creeper (0.49), Small Indian Mongoose (0.47).

conservation_priority.text: Top experimental CIPI grid cells in West Bengal (equal-weight reference): cell near 22.875N 88.125E (overall rank 1, median rank across weightings 6); cell near 22.875N 87.375E (overall rank 3, median rank across weightings 8); cell near 23.625N 87.375E (overall rank 22, median rank across weightings 37).

environmental_pressures.text: Tree cover of at least 30% canopy covered 4,476 km2 (5.06% of land) in 2000 (Hansen Global Forest Change; includes plantations).

161.2 km2 of that tree cover was lost in 2001-2024 (3.6% of the 2000 extent; 0.88% in 2015-2024, rank 13 of 35 states). The largest annual loss was in 2010 (20.82 km2). Loss includes plantation harvest and natural disturbance; regrowth is not subtracted.
Built-up surfaces cover 2.31% of land and population density is 1,182.9 people per km2 (GHSL 2020).
34% of 30 m tree-cover pixels lie on a forest edge (a fragmentation indicator; higher means more fragmented).
These describe pressures on places; they do not show effects on any species.

sources: Hansen et al. Global Forest Change 2000-2024 v1.12 (CC BY 4.0)
GHSL R2023A built-up and population 2020 (CC BY 4.0)
